name: Custom block-cipher mode analysis: decryption, parallelizability, bit-flip propagation, IND-CPA
identify_givens: A made-up mode of operation (AES-SEC, AES-MIX, AES-MOD, or a 'novel mode') defined by encryption recurrences: a special formula for $C_1$ (sometimes also $C_2$) plus a general recurrence $C_i = E_K(\cdots)$ mixing $P_i$, IVs, and earlier ciphertext/plaintext blocks via XOR. Block size $n$ is given; message $P = (P_1,\dots,P_m)$ is a multiple of $n$ so no padding is needed. $E_K$ is a secure block cipher (e.g. AES) with shared key $K$; $D_K$ may be used in answers. One or two IVs $IV_1, IV_2$ are chosen and sent in the clear as $(IV_1, IV_2, C_1, \dots, C_m)$; the IVs may be stated as random/independent or constant/reused.
identify_target: (1) Derive an efficient decryption formula for $P_i$ (sometimes specifically $P_1$, $P_2$, or $i > 2$) using $D_K$; (2) state whether encryption and decryption can be parallelized, with justification from data dependencies; (3) compute what Bob decrypts after a single-bit flip in one ciphertext block, marking garbage blocks and exact bit-flip propagation; (4) justify or break IND-CPA security (counterexample pair of messages if IVs are reused/constant, informal justification if random).
strategy_name: Invert-Isolate-Trace: algebraically invert the recurrence, then read dependencies and error paths off the decryption formula

algorithm.detail: Write out the given encryption equations and mark, for each $C_i$, which terms enter the block cipher input (inside $E_K(\cdot)$) and which are only XORed outside. E.g. AES-MIX: $C_1 = E_K(IV_1 \oplus P_1)$, $C_2 = E_K(IV_2 \oplus P_2) \oplus C_1$, $C_i = E_K(C_{i-2} \oplus P_i)$ for $i > 2$. This inside/outside split drives everything later.
XOR both sides of the equation with every term that sits outside $E_K$, so $E_K(\text{input})$ stands alone on one side. For AES-MIX $C_2$: $C_2 \oplus C_1 = E_K(IV_2 \oplus P_2)$.

Apply $D_K$ to both sides to expose the block cipher input, then XOR the remaining mask over to isolate $P_i$. AES-MIX: $D_K(C_2 \oplus C_1) = IV_2 \oplus P_2$, so $P_2 = D_K(C_2 \oplus C_1) \oplus IV_2$; and $C_i = E_K(C_{i-2} \oplus P_i)$ gives $P_i = D_K(C_i) \oplus C_{i-2}$. Repeat separately for each special case ($P_1$, $P_2$).

Inspect data dependencies in each formula. Encryption is parallelizable only if $C_i$ needs no earlier ciphertext; it is sequential when $C_i$ depends on $C_{i-1}$ (AES-SEC), $C_{i-2}$ (AES-MIX), or $C_1 \oplus \cdots \oplus C_{i-1}$ (AES-MOD). Decryption is parallelizable only if $P_i$ depends solely on ciphertext blocks and IVs (AES-MIX: yes; AES-MOD: yes). Watch for plaintext feedback: AES-SEC's $P_i = D_K(C_i \oplus P_{i-1}) \oplus C_{i-1}$ needs $P_{i-1}$, so decryption is also sequential.

For tampered $C_j' = C_j \oplus 1$, evaluate every $P_i'$ using the decryption formula. Rule: if the corrupted block enters $D_K(\cdot)$, that plaintext block is garbage (avalanche of the block cipher); if it appears only as an XOR term, the same single-bit flip passes through to $P_i' = P_i \oplus 1$. Blocks whose decryption formula never references $C_j$ are unchanged.

Check the IV: if IVs are constant or reused across messages, the mode is deterministic — break it by querying two messages sharing a first block ($P_1;P_2$ vs $P_1;P_3$) and comparing the first ciphertext blocks for equality. If fresh independent random IVs per message randomize every ciphertext block (and chaining prevents identical encryptions), argue IND-CPA secure informally.

variations.name: Plaintext feedback kills decryption parallelism
variations.detail: AES-SEC (exam-with-solutions.pdf::1) uses $C_i = E_K(P_i \oplus C_{i-1}) \oplus P_{i-1}$, so decryption $P_i = D_K(C_i \oplus P_{i-1}) \oplus C_{i-1}$ needs the *previous plaintext* — both encryption AND decryption are sequential. Trap: assuming decryption is always parallel as in CBC. Adapt Step 4 by checking for $P_{i-1}$ terms in the decryption formula, not just ciphertext terms.

variations.name: Bit-flip propagation vs garbage reversed by formula shape
variations.detail: In AES-MIX a flip in $C_1$ makes $P_1', P_2'$ garbage (both push $C_1'$ through $D_K$) but gives $P_3' = P_3 \oplus 1$ (XOR-only use). In AES-MOD a flip in $C_2$ makes $P_2'$ garbage while $P_3', P_4'$ each flip exactly one bit ($C_2$ is XORed into every later decryption) and $P_1$ is intact. Adapt Step 5 by expanding each $P_i'$ concretely instead of quoting CBC intuition.

variations.name: Constant IV / determinism instead of IV reuse
variations.detail: The re-exam 'novel mode' (re-exam-problems-with-sample-solutions.pdf::8) uses a hard-coded constant $c_0$ and $E_K(K)$, making encryption deterministic: not IND-CPA even without an explicit reuse assumption; the fix is a fresh random IV whose randomness propagates through all $c_i$. Adapt Step 6 to first check whether *any* randomness exists at all before discussing reuse.

variations.name: Self-correcting / finite error propagation asked instead of IND-CPA
variations.detail: The same re-exam problem asks whether the mode is self-correcting: with $m_i = c_i \oplus E_K(c_{i-2}) \oplus E_K(c_{i-1})$, an error in $c_4$ corrupts exactly $m_4, m_5, m_6$ (three blocks, since $c_4$ is referenced by decryption of blocks 4–6) and nothing before or after. Adapt Step 5 into: list every decryption equation containing the corrupted block; those blocks are wrong, all others correct; if the set is finite the mode self-corrects.

example_problem: Alice and Bob design the AES-MIX mode of operation: $C_1 = E_K(IV_1 \oplus P_1)$; $C_2 = E_K(IV_2 \oplus P_2) \oplus C_1$; $C_i = E_K(C_{i-2} \oplus P_i)$ for $i > 2$, where $E_K$ is a secure block cipher (e.g. AES) with key $K$ shared by Alice and Bob. The message $P = (P_1, \dots, P_m)$ has blocks of size $n$ and is a multiple of $n$ (no padding). Alice chooses two independent random IVs and sends $(IV_1, IV_2, C_1, \dots, C_m)$. (1a) Derive an efficient decryption formula for $P_2$ and for $P_i$, $i > 2$, using $D_K$. (1b) Explain whether the encryption and decryption formulas can be parallelized. (1c) A network error flips a single bit of the first ciphertext block of a 3-block message, $C_1' = C_1 \oplus 1$; show what message Bob computes when decrypting $C' = (IV_1, IV_2, C_1', C_2, C_3)$, justifying garbage output and computing exact results otherwise.

example_steps.work: Structure map: for $C_1$ and the general $C_i$, everything except $P_i$/$IV_1$ sits inside $E_K$; for $C_2$ there is an extra XOR with $C_1$ outside the cipher. So $C_1$ and $C_i$ invert with one $D_K$ plus one XOR, while $C_2$ needs $C_1$ XORed off first.

Isolate $E_K$ terms. For $P_2$: $C_2 = E_K(IV_2 \oplus P_2) \oplus C_1 \Rightarrow C_2 \oplus C_1 = E_K(IV_2 \oplus P_2)$. For $P_i$, $i>2$: $C_i = E_K(C_{i-2} \oplus P_i)$ already has $E_K$ isolated. For $P_1$: $C_1 = E_K(IV_1 \oplus P_1)$ likewise.

Apply $D_K$ and solve: $D_K(C_2 \oplus C_1) = IV_2 \oplus P_2 \Rightarrow P_2 = D_K(C_2 \oplus C_1) \oplus IV_2$. And $D_K(C_i) = C_{i-2} \oplus P_i \Rightarrow P_i = D_K(C_i) \oplus C_{i-2}$ for $i > 2$ (matches the official solution). Also $P_1 = D_K(C_1) \oplus IV_1$.

Encryption cannot be parallelized: computing $C_i$ requires knowing $C_{i-2}$ (and $C_2$ requires $C_1$). Decryption can be parallelized: $P_i = D_K(C_i) \oplus C_{i-2}$ uses only ciphertext blocks, which are all available to Bob — it does not require knowing any of $P_1, \dots, P_{i-1}$.

Decrypt $C' = (IV_1, IV_2, C_1 \oplus 1, C_2, C_3)$. $P_1' = D_K(C_1') \oplus IV_1 = D_K(C_1 \oplus 1) \oplus IV_1 = \text{Garbage}$: the corrupted block enters $D_K$, and AES avalanche makes the output unpredictable. $P_2' = D_K(C_2 \oplus C_1') \oplus IV_2 = D_K(C_2 \oplus C_1 \oplus 1) \oplus IV_2 = \text{Garbage}$: $C_1'$ again enters $D_K$ via the XOR inside. $P_3' = D_K(C_3) \oplus C_1' = D_K(C_3) \oplus C_1 \oplus 1 = P_3 \oplus 1$: here $C_1$ is only XORed after decryption, so exactly the flipped bit propagates. Bob recovers $P_3$ with one bit flipped; blocks 1 and 2 are garbage.

IND-CPA (not asked in this instance, but per algorithm): AES-MIX picks fresh independent random $IV_1, IV_2$ per message, so equal plaintexts encrypt to different ciphertexts and the first-block equality attack fails; the mode is IND-CPA secure. Contrast with AES-SEC under reused IVs, where messages $P_1;P_2$ and $P_1;P_3$ yield identical first ciphertext blocks, breaking IND-CPA.
